questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials cannot be transported in a trailer with:

options.text: A heater.
An air conditioner.
Other items.
Batteries.

questions.correctAnswerText: A heater.
questions.explanation: Heaters are not allowed when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they confirm that the package:

options.text: Does not contain hazardous materials.
Has been prepared following all rules.
Was packed at a specific location.
Will be placed on the trailer first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has been prepared following all rules.
questions.explanation: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they certify that the package has been prepared according to all applicable rules.

questions.question: Shippers package hazardous materials in order to ____ them.

options.text: Contain
Release
Insulate

questions.correctAnswerText: Contain
questions.explanation: Shippers package hazardous materials to keep them contained. Vehicles must be labeled to show the danger of the cargo.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is a good way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?

options.text: Talking to other drivers
Attending hazardous materials training courses
Guessing
Working on cars

questions.correctAnswerText: Attending hazardous materials training courses
questions.explanation: The manual helps you pass the written exam, but it does not cover everything needed to do the job safely. Training courses provide additional knowledge about transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: The National Response Center must be notified of an incident with all of the following, except:

options.text: Death.
Injury requiring hospitalization.
Injury not requiring hospitalization.

questions.correctAnswerText: Injury not requiring hospitalization.
questions.explanation: Report to the National Response Center if there is death, hospitalization, property damage of $50,000 or more, evacuation of the public, closure of a major transportation route for more than one hour, or fire, spillage, or contamination involving radiation, bacteria, or toxins. You should also report if the situation seems serious enough.

questions.question: A person supervising the loading of a tank:

options.text: Should be certified in CPR.
Must be a licensed firefighter.
Does not need to know the materials being loaded.
Must stay within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stay within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A qualified person must watch the loading of a tank. This person must stay alert, see the tank clearly, stay within 25 feet, know the hazards of the materials, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: Shipping papers should be:

options.text: Hidden from view.
Placed in the glove box.
Easily visible to anyone entering the cab.
Laminated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Easily visible to anyone entering the cab.
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or another location you can reach easily while wearing your seat belt. They must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: A sign that your shipment contains hazardous materials is:

options.text: The shipper works in a business that uses hazardous materials, like fireworks or pest control.
Your last shipment was labeled as hazardous.
The packaging looks damaged.
The shipper's business is in a bad neighborhood.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper works in a business that uses hazardous materials, like fireworks or pest control.
questions.explanation: One clue that a shipment may contain hazardous materials is the type of business. Businesses that work with hazardous materials include paint dealers, chemical supply companies, and pest control firms.

questions.question: What does a hazardous materials shipping paper describe?

options.text: The materials being transported
How the materials will be transported
Who should accept the materials being transported
The cost of the materials

questions.correctAnswerText: The materials being transported
questions.explanation: A shipping paper describes the hazardous materials being transported. Examples include shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests.

questions.question: What is the symbol for a marine pollutant?

options.text: Waves in a yellow triangle with an X through the waves
A fish in a white triangle with an X through the fish
A light blue square with a dark blue X through it
A bird in a red octagon

questions.correctAnswerText: A fish in a white triangle with an X through the fish
questions.explanation: The marine pollutant symbol is a fish in a white triangle with an X through the fish.

questions.question: If hazardous materials cargo is leaking and the driver has no phone, what should they do?

options.text: Drive to find a phone to call emergency personnel.
Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility.
Send someone else to get help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Send someone else to get help.
questions.explanation: Do not move your vehicle when hazardous materials leak. Moving it spreads contamination over a larger area. Park your vehicle, secure it, stay with it, and call emergency personnel. If you have no phone, send someone else to get help.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous materials label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the package.
Attach a QR code to scan instead.
Make the HazMat label smaller to fit on the package.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: If a hazardous materials label does not fit on a package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: Where should hazardous materials shipping papers NOT be kept?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's door.
In a pouch on the passenger's door.
Within the driver's reach while wearing a seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's door.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be easy to reach in an emergency. Keep them in a pouch on the driver's door or within easy reach while your seat belt is fastened. You can keep them on the driver's seat when you are not in the vehicle.

questions.question: Can you abbreviate identification numbers, shipping names, and hazard classes on shipping papers?

options.text: Yes, if the paper is small.
Yes, to make them easier to read.
No, never abbreviate them.
Yes, if the abbreviations are easy to understand.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never abbreviate them.
questions.explanation: Never abbreviate identification numbers, shipping names, or hazard classes on shipping papers. The only exception is if the abbreviation is allowed by hazardous materials regulations.

questions.question: Which sign suggests cargo contains hazardous materials?

options.text: Cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
Cargo is picked up from a supermarket.
Cargo is packed in cardboard boxes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Packaging type can show if materials are hazardous. Cylinders and drums are commonly used to store and transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: If a shipping paper has both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, how should they be listed?

options.text: Hazardous materials must be listed first.
Hazardous materials must be written larger.
Hazardous materials must be written in red ink.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazardous materials must be listed first.
questions.explanation: When a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, list the hazardous materials first.

questions.question: What shape are placards that show hazardous materials in a vehicle?

options.text: A tall rectangle
A triangle
A diamond

questions.correctAnswerText: A diamond
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: If your vehicle with explosives breaks down, how should you warn other drivers?

options.text: Use flares.
Use reflective triangles.
Stand on the road and wave your arms.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use reflective triangles.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives, use reflective triangles or red electric lights for warning signals. Never use burning signals like flares or fuses with explosives.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous materials label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the package.
Attach a scannable QR code to the package instead.
Reduce the size of the HazMat label to fit on the package.
Paste the label on the trailer wall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: If a hazardous materials label will not fit on a package, place it on a tag that is securely attached to the package.

questions.question: What must you do to complete a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest?

options.text: Sign by hand.
Sign only if you cross into another state.
Sign only if the weather was hazardous.
Have a witness sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sign by hand.
questions.explanation: A Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest must be signed by hand. Include the name and EPA registration number of all shippers, carriers, and destinations on the manifest.

questions.question: When transporting radioactive materials, you should know:

options.text: Radiation spreads around the package and passes through to other packages nearby.
The package should be transported in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation spreads around the package and passes through to other packages nearby.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads around each radioactive package and passes through to nearby packages. How many packages can be loaded together is controlled.

questions.question: To apply for a HazMat endorsement, which agency must perform a background check on you?

options.text: The Transportation Security Administration
The Federal Bureau of Investigation
The Department of Energy
The Department of Defense

questions.correctAnswerText: The Transportation Security Administration
questions.explanation: To get or renew a hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass a background check from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: When transporting hazardous materials, placards:

options.text: Should be lit up.
Should be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.
Should be used only by Class A licensed drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle when required.

questions.question: When transporting mass explosives:

options.text: The vehicle must always be placarded.
The vehicle only needs to be placarded if carrying more than 200 pounds.
The vehicle does not need to be placarded.
Only rural roads should be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle must always be placarded.
questions.explanation: Some hazardous materials only need placards if 1,001 pounds or more are being carried. But mass explosives always require placards, no matter how much is being carried.

questions.question: The correct way to check tire pressure is by:

options.text: Using a tire pressure gauge.
Looking at the tires.
Pushing on the tires to feel how hard they are.
Weighing the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using a tire pressure gauge.
questions.explanation: Check each tire at the start of every trip. A tire pressure gauge is the only reliable way to check tire pressure.

questions.question: Hazardous materials may be transported by:

options.text: Any driver with a CDL.
A driver with a CDL and a hazardous materials endorsement.
Any driver in rural areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver with a CDL and a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle used to transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: When transporting chlorine, what must be in the vehicle?

options.text: A gas mask
Goggles
An axe

questions.correctAnswerText: A gas mask
questions.explanation: An approved gas mask must be in the vehicle when transporting chlorine in cargo tanks.

questions.question: Shippers must label hazardous materials. If an item is too small for a label, how should it be labeled?

options.text: Tie it with other hazardous materials and put a warning label sheet on the outside of the bundle.
Attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
Mark the item with a large orange dot.
Place the item in a box that displays a warning label.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attach the label to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped hazard labels must be placed on most hazardous materials packages. If the label won't fit on the package, it can be placed on a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: To complete a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest, you must:

options.text: Sign the manifest by hand.
Only sign the manifest if you cross into another state.
Have a witness sign the manifest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sign the manifest by hand.
questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous waste, you must carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest. It must be signed by hand.

questions.question: Hazardous materials laws are controlled by:

options.text: Local regulations.
State regulations.
Federal regulations.
All levels of government.

questions.correctAnswerText: All levels of government.
questions.explanation: Because hazardous materials are dangerous, federal, state, and local governments can all create rules for transporting them.
